data.title: Mahanadi Coalfields shares make flat listing at 2% discount to IPO price; here’s how to trade Coal India unit
data.description:
Mahanadi Coalfields shares were listed on the exchanges on November 27.

Shares of Coal India unit Mahanadi Coalfields fell more than 2 percent in their trading debut on Friday, following a 1.52-times subscription to its initial public offering (IPO) in the primary market between November 19 and 23.

Shares of Mahanadi Coalfields were listed at Rs 133.15 per share on the BSE, a discount of 2.10 percent. The company's market capitalisation post-listing of its shares stood at Rs 88,123.50 crore.

On the NSE, the shares of the company were listed at Rs 134 per share, discount of 1.47 percent. The Rs 8,981 crore initial share sale had a price band of Rs 129-136 per share.

Earlier, the company raised Rs 2,295 crore from anchor investors.

The proposed listing is part of Coal India's broader plan to unlock value from its subsidiaries through the capital markets.

MCL is the third Coal India subsidiary to tap the public markets this year. Coal India has already listed Bharat Coking Coal Ltd in January, while the IPO of Central Mine Planning & Design Institute Ltd concluded in March.

Incorporated in 1992, MCL produced 218.31 million tonnes of coal in FY26, accounting for around 22.4 per cent of India's total non-coking coal production, according to the Crisil report cited in the offer documents.

It is also the largest coal-producing subsidiary of Coal India, contributing over 28 per cent to the state-owned company's total coal production in FY26.

Coal India accounts for more than 80 per cent of the country's domestic coal output.

data.title: Buzzing Stocks: Kalyan Jewellers jumps 2% on HSBC's 'Buy' call; IGI gains 3% after block deal
data.description:
Buzzing Stocks

Stock-specific activity is likely to remain in focus on Dalal Street on November 27,  following a slew of block deals, corporate developments, brokerage calls and other company-specific triggers.

Kalyan Jewellers shares jumped 2 percent after HSBC maintained 'Buy' rating with a target price of Rs 830 per share, highlighting its affordable gold jewellery-focused ATM brand with competitive making charges. The brokerage has not factored ATM into its estimates, and strong execution could provide upside. Demand trends remain strong despite a high base.

Shares of International Gemological Institute gained 3 percent after 67.16 lakh shares worth Rs 280 crore change hands at Rs 417/share in block deal window.

Shares of Waaree Renewable Technologies rose 12 percent after the company received a Letter of Award (LOA) for a 120 MWp turnkey project involving module supply and execution of engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) works.

Shares of ABS Marine Services added 4 percent after the company received a Notification of Award (NOA) from Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) for the charter hire of its platform supply vessel, 'Emerald', for three years. The contract is valued at approximately Rs 120.14 crore.

Investors are expected to remain focused on brokerage calls, block deals, order wins, regulatory developments and other company-specific triggers that could drive stock-level volatility during the session.

Shares of Kalyan Jewellers India rose 3.3 percent to Rs 661 in morning trade on Friday, November 27, after HSBC said jewellery demand remained strong despite a high base. The brokerage also cited the growth potential of the retailer’s affordable gold jewellery brand, Akshaya Thanga Maligai (ATM).

Kalyan Jewellers was among the top midcap gainers, with a market capitalisation of about Rs 68,300 crore. The stock has gained 36.9 percent so far this year, while the benchmark Nifty 50 has declined 1.2 percent.

HSBC has a Buy rating on Kalyan Jewellers and a target price of Rs 830 per share, implying about 30 percent upside from Thursday’s close. The brokerage highlighted ATM’s competitive making charges and said strong execution at the brand could lift earnings above its current estimates, which exclude ATM’s contribution.

The stock also rallied earlier this week, after Moneycontrol reported that Kalyan Jewellers was in talks with several private equity firms, including former investor Warburg Pincus, to raise close to Rs 2,000 crore through minority stake sales in its subsidiaries Candere and ATM.

A deal with Warburg Pincus would bring the private equity firm back into the Kalyan group more than two years after it completed its exit from the listed retailer in August 2024. Warburg Pincus invested about Rs 1,700 crore in two rounds between 2014 and 2017, helping Kalyan Jewellers expand from its South Indian base into northern and western India as well as overseas markets.

Kalyan Jewellers Q2 profit rises 64%

Kalyan Jewellers reported a 63.6 percent year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 427 crore for the September quarter, from Rs 260.51 crore a year earlier. The quarter included a Rs 73 crore exceptional gain from the sale of a non-core land parcel. Excluding that gain, net profit rose nearly 36 percent to about Rs 354 crore.

Consolidated revenue rose 31.4 percent to Rs 10,323 crore from Rs 7,856 crore a year earlier, crossing the Rs 10,000 crore mark. Following the results, UBS maintained its Buy rating on the stock with a target price of Rs 900 per share.

data.title: SME issue: Airpro Tech IPO to open today for subscription; check bid price, allotment date, other key details
data.description:
IPO latest updates

Airpro Technology India initial public offering (IPO) will open for public subscription on November 27 at 10 am in the primary market, aiming to raise Rs 35.64 crore.

The SME issue comprises up to 36 lakh equity shares with a face value of Rs 10 each at an issue price of Rs 99 per share. It includes a fresh issue of up to 29.20 lakh equity shares and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 6.80 lakh equity shares by the selling shareholders.

The issue will close on December 1. The company's shares will be listed on the NSE Emerge platform.

The company plans to utilise the net proceeds from the IPO to purchase machinery for its manufacturing facility, make the balance payment for acquiring land for a factory in Jaipur, construct the factory building, meet working capital requirements and for general corporate purposes.

Horizon Management Private Ltd is the lead manager to the issue, while MUFG Intime India Private Ltd is the registrar.

Headquartered in Jaipur, Rajasthan, Airpro Technology India operates as a brand owner through a hybrid business model that includes product design, firmware customisation, cloud-enabled network management, in-house assembly and white-label networking solutions.

The company undertakes the assembly and testing of its access point devices at its facility in Goregaon East, Mumbai.

Its product portfolio includes wireless access points, WLAN controllers, Ethernet switches, gateways, outdoor wireless solutions, 4G/5G customer premises equipment (CPE) and industrial PoE switches. It also offers a cloud-based network management platform called AirproCloud.

data.title: Shares find footing after bruising month, dollar set for third monthly gain
data.description:
The US dollar was headed to its third monthly gain on Friday
  • Asian shares steady after a tough month amid AI jitters.
  • US dollar heads toward its third consecutive monthly gain.
  • Oil prices are set for their first weekly rise in four.
Did our AI summary help?

Asian shares were set to end a bruising month on a steadier note as a holiday lull offered some respite from AI jitters, while the dollar reigned supreme, riding a wave of safe-haven demand and rate hike bets towards a third month of gains.

Oil prices were headed for the first weekly rise in four on renewed concerns about supply disruptions. Brent crude futures slipped 0.4% on Friday to $96.14 a barrel, but were still up 3.9% for the week. For the month, they were down 18%.

Wall Street was closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday, but in Asia, S&P 500 futures were up 0.8% and Nasdaq futures were 1% higher.

Japan's Nikkei rose 0.7% to bring its gains for the week to 2.7%, clawing back only a fraction of its 8.4% loss for the month. Data showed on Friday that core inflation in Tokyo hit a 16-month high in November, bolstering the case for an interest rate hike from the Bank of Japan as soon as next month.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan edged up 0.5% to end the week 1.9% higher. It was still down 8.2% for the month.

Related Stories

  • KOSPI plunges 5.3%, Nikkei falls 2.9% as Nvidia-led tech rally fizzles; US tariff fears hit Asian ma...
  • KOSPI surges 7.5%, Nikkei jumps 5%, Taiwan rallies 9% as Nvidia-led AI stock rebound sweeps Asian ma...
  • South Korea says market measures will ease investor jitters

Shares in South Korea rallied 2% and China's blue chips slipped 0.2%, after hitting the lowest level since June 2025 a day earlier.

"Barring a big shock that severely rattles a thin market, November is practically in the books and the markets limp into December where a seasonal 'Santa Rally' currently appears elusive," said Kyle Rodda, a senior analyst at Capital.com.

"For as long as the markets remain unsure about the growth trajectory for AI and lack clarity about where US rates may peak, uncertainty and therefore volatility is liable to remain elevated."

Tech giant Nvidia remained a source of unease after S&P put its credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade. The chipmaker told manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers containing its chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, the Financial Times reported.

Elsewhere in tech, Elon Musk said that every child in the US would receive two shares in his space and AI company SpaceX, pledging a gift worth some $18 billion.

Dollar reigns

The US dollar was headed to its third monthly gain on Friday, up 1.8% against its major peers at 103.8. It has been supported by expectations that the Federal Reserve is almost certain to lift interest rates in December, as well as safe-haven flows from the selloff in equities.

Futures imply a 99% chance the Fed will raise rates by 25 basis points in December, but speculation of a half-point increase has faded.

The euro was last flat at $1.0964, after news that Spanish central banking veteran Pablo Hernández de Cos would become the next European Central Bank president, a move that was well telegraphed and suggested policy continuity.

The kiwi edged up 0.2% to $0.5482 after New Zealand's ruling centre-right coalition fell short of a parliamentary majority, leaving it reliant on negotiations with the centrist Opportunity Party to stay in power.

Bond investors are wondering if the broad losses in global stocks this month coupled with doubts about the durability of AI-driven business investment might temper the hawkishness of central banks.

"The Fed could, of course, still blink," said David Rees, chief economist at Schroders. "But a Fed put would not necessarily be unambiguously positive for markets."

"If growth and inflation data remain firm, in a game of cat and mouse markets could soon begin pricing a more hawkish Fed back in, potentially setting off the same chain of events all over again."

Two-year Treasury yields rose 3 basis points to 4.6705% as the cash market reopened after the US holiday. They were up 6 bps this week.

Benchmark 10-year Treasury yields rose 4 bps to 4.8918%, but were down 2 bps for the week.

data.title: Currency Check | Rupee opens 6 paise lower at 92.50 per dollar
data.description:
The Indian rupee opened lower by 6 paise on November 27, at 92.50 per dollar, compared with Wednesday's close of 92.44.

According to Finrex, dollar is expected to open at 92.50 against the rupee a tad stronger with month end demand crossing the > Rs. 5000 crores of buying by FPIs in equities yesterday. So initially we may see the pair moving lower but may then slowly move higher towards 92.75 depending on how much of month end demand has been met yesterday.

On Monday we will be having the $ 2 bio flows of MSCI rebalancing. Exporters to sell the upticks that they get while importers to buy the dips, it added.

Asian currencies traded mixed against the US dollar in early trade, with the Indonesian rupiah declining 0.17 percent, followed by the Thai baht, which slipped 0.07 percent. The Malaysian ringgit and Singapore dollar edged lower by 0.03 percent and 0.01 percent, respectively. Meanwhile, the Japanese yen eased 0.02 percent. On the other hand, the Chinese renminbi strengthened 0.15 percent, while the Taiwan dollar and Philippine peso gained 0.05 percent and 0.04 percent, respectively. The South Korean won edged higher by 0.01 percent.

The US dollar hovered below a 22-month peak in holiday-thinned trading on Friday, with traders looking to equity markets for clues on direction as doubts about the AI trade triggers heightened volatility.
